content.text: Now I'll read all order lines, which questions 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 depend on.
I have the raw data; now I'll confirm the derived answers with the store's own queries, starting with Harbor Supplies' orders via the placed_by relation.

input.statement: MATCH (o:order)-[:placed_by]->(c:customer {name: $name}) RETURN o.id, o.placed_on, o.total, o.status ORDER BY o.placed_on
MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order {id: $id}), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product)-[:supplied_by]->(s:supplier) RETURN l.id, p.sku, p.name, l.qty, s.name, s.country ORDER BY l.id
MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order {id: $id}), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) RETURN l.id, p.sku, p.name, l.qty ORDER BY l.id
MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status = 'open' AND p.category = 'valves' RETURN o.id, l.id, p.sku, p.name ORDER BY o.id

content.text: Next I'll aggregate orders per customer (Q5), category units excluding cancelled (Q6), and find never-ordered products (Q9), all in one batch.

input.statement: MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' RETURN p.category, sum(l.qty) AS units ORDER BY p.category
MATCH (p:product) WHERE NOT (p)<-[:of_product]-(:order_line) RETURN p.sku, p.name, p.category

content.text: The refusal says aggregate groups come ordered by key on their own, so I'll drop the ORDER BY and rerun the category sum.

input.statement: MATCH (l:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o:order), (l)-[:of_product]->(p:product) WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' RETURN p.category, sum(l.qty) AS units

content.text: That matches my hand sum. For Q7 I'll read the ranking five lines at a time, sorted by qty descending with id as a tiebreaker so ties are deterministic.
I'll follow the cursor to read ranks 6–10.
For Q8, I'll check for a shared product between the two customers, since the shortest possible link is customer→order→line→product←line←order←customer.

input.statement: MATCH (a:customer {name: $a})<-[:placed_by]-(o1:order)<-[:of_order]-(l1:order_line)-[:of_product]->(p:product)<-[:of_product]-(l2:order_line)-[:of_order]->(o2:order)-[:placed_by]->(b:customer {name: $b}) RETURN o1.id, l1.id, p.sku, p.name, l2.id, o2.id

content.text:
I answered all nine questions. Every read was pinned to position 74 of the `trade` lake, so all the answers come from the same snapshot. No records were retired.

**1. Harbor Supplies (C-2) has placed three orders.** I read these through the order → customer link.

| Order | Date | Total | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1002 | 2026-08-11 | 372.00 | shipped |
| O-1006 | 2026-09-09 | 142.50 | open |
| O-1011 | 2026-10-13 | 144.00 | cancelled |

**2. Order O-1007 has two products:**
- P-21, Check valve DN25: 2 units (line L-1007-1)
- P-40, O-ring set: 8 units (line L-1007-2)

**3. Three suppliers make the products on order O-1004:**
- **Lago Valvole (S-2), Italy (IT):** P-20 Ball valve DN25
- **Torino Guarnizioni (S-4), Italy (IT):** P-40 O-ring set and P-41 Gasket DN25
- **Nordic Fasteners (S-1), Sweden (SE):** P-10 Hex bolt M8

**4. Three open orders contain a valve:**
- O-1004 has P-20 Ball valve (line L-1004-1).
- O-1007 has P-21 Check valve (line L-1007-1).
- O-1009 has P-20 Ball valve (line L-1009-2).

The other open orders (O-1006, O-1010 and O-1012) have no valves.

**5. Orders per customer, counting every status:**

| Customer | Orders | Total |
|---|---|---|
| C-1 Delta Metals | 3 | 1653.00 |
| C-2 Harbor Supplies | 3 | 658.50 |
| C-3 Brightwater Utilities | 2 | 2611.50 |
| C-4 Kestrel Farms | 2 | 247.00 |
| C-5 Ostrava Machining | 2 | 1035.00 |
| C-6 Vale Hardware | 0 | 0 |

The store's grouped totals match the 12 order records. Vale Hardware doesn't appear in those totals because it has no orders.

**6. Units per category, leaving out the cancelled orders O-1005 and O-1011:**
- fasteners: 4490
- seals: 163
- valves: 25
- pumps: 14

My first query was refused because the store won't sort grouped results, so I reran it without sorting. The results match my own sum from the 27 order lines.

**7. Ranks 6 to 10 by quantity.** I read the ranking five lines at a time, highest quantity first. Lines with the same quantity are ordered by id: L-1001-1 and L-1001-2 both have 400 and sit at ranks 4 and 5.

| Rank | Line | Order | Product | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | L-1012-2 | O-1012 | P-12 | 300 |
| 7 | L-1006-2 | O-1006 | P-11 | 250 |
| 8 | L-1006-1 | O-1006 | P-10 | 200 |
| 9 | L-1004-4 | O-1004 | P-10 | 150 |
| 10 | L-1012-1 | O-1012 | P-10 | 90 |

Ranks 1 to 5 were L-1008-1 (1200), L-1001-3 (800), L-1010-1 (700), L-1001-1 (400) and L-1001-2 (400).

**8. Kestrel Farms and Ostrava Machining both ordered Washer M8 (P-12).** The shortest chain is:

Kestrel Farms (C-4) ← order O-1012 ← line L-1012-2 → product P-12 Washer M8 ← line L-1008-1 → order O-1008 → Ostrava Machining (C-5)

That is seven records and six links. Nothing shorter is possible: each order belongs to one customer, so two customers can only meet through a product they both ordered. The store found exactly one such path.

**9. Two products have never been ordered:**
- P-13 Threaded rod M8 (fasteners)
- P-42 Shaft seal 30mm (seals)

I checked this with a query for products that no order line points to, and the full list of 27 lines agrees.
